title: Canadian Commuter E-Bike Comparison
subtitle: Seven commuter e-bikes you can buy in Canada for CAD $1,699-$3,499, with specs taken from each maker's own product page.
currency_note: Every price below was read from the maker's Canadian storefront in Canadian dollars (CAD). Specs were read from the maker's own product/spec pages on the date above.

products.warranty: 2 years frame, components and battery; 1 year some items (Rad warranty page)
products.best_for: A long, bike-feeling commute: the torque sensor and 100 Nm motor make pedalling feel assisted rather than motorised. It is the heaviest bike here, so it suits a garage or ground-floor lock-up.
products.source_note: Technical Specifications block on the product page (Samsung 50GB / LG M50LT cells, UL 2271). Price from the product's Shopify .js endpoint, CAD. Re-read 2026-10-08: CA$2,699.00 CAD, in stock, Reg. 74.5 lb (33.8 kg), 100 Nm, 320 lb (145 kg) / 290 lb rider, 15 Ah 720 Wh. Re-verified 2026-10-09 against the live page: CA$2,699.00 CAD, 500 W / 100 Nm, 15Ah 720 Wh, 40-104 km, 74.5 lb, hydraulic disc, Class 1/2 shipping Class 2, torque sensor, 320 lb / 290 lb rider - all unchanged. Rad's own warranty page (read 2026-10-09) publishes 2 years for frame, components and battery and 1 year for pedals, freewheel, crankset, cassette, derailleur, shifter and saddle, so the warranty cell now reads 2 years.

products.warranty: 2 years frame, components and battery; 1 year some items (Rad warranty page)
products.best_for: Short trips and stairs: Rad's lightest bike at 55 lb, with a rear rack rated 55 lb. The small 360 Wh battery is the trade-off - it is the shortest-range bike in this set.
products.source_note: Technical Specifications / Geometry blocks on the product page (UL-2271 battery). Price from the product's Shopify .js endpoint, CAD. Re-read 2026-10-08: CA$1,899.00 CAD, in stock, 55 lb (25.2 kg), 40 Nm, 300 lb (136 kg) / 275 lb rider, 10 Ah 360 Wh, Class 2. Re-verified 2026-10-09 against the live page: CA$1,899.00 CAD, 500 W / 40 Nm, 10Ah 360 Wh, 24-56 km, 55 lb, hydraulic disc (Gemma GA-950), Class 2, cadence sensor, 300 lb / 275 lb rider - all unchanged. Warranty now read from Rad's own warranty page (2026-10-09) as 2 years frame/components/battery.

products.best_for: Carrying-up-stairs and mixed bike/motor use: at 39 lb it is by far the lightest here, and light enough to ride with the motor off. The 374 Wh battery is the smallest, so plan short hops or charge often.
products.source_note: Key Features block and the Specification & Geometry table on the product page. Price shown as CA$2,099.00 CAD on the product page. Re-read 2026-10-08: the spec table now publishes Ebike Class 1/2/3 (default 32 km/h, adjustable 19-45) and Max Bike Load Capacity 150 kg, so those cells are no longer 'not stated'. Re-verified 2026-10-09 against the live page: CA$2,099.00 CAD, 36V 350W / 650W peak / 45Nm, 36V 10.14Ah (374Wh), pedal-assist range 97 km, 17.7 kg, Shimano hydraulic disc 180 mm both ends, Class 1/2/3 (32 km/h default, adjustable 19-45), torque and cadence sensor, max bike load 150 kg - all unchanged.

products.payload: 440 lb max bike load / 66 lb rack
products.best_for: The all-round daily commuter: a 750 W motor, a 730 Wh battery and the second-longest claimed range here (~129 km of pedal assist), with lights, fenders and a rear rack included. It ships as Class 2; Class 3 (28 mph) is unlocked in the app where local rules allow.
products.source_note: Specification & Geometry table on the product page. Price shown as CA$2,699.00 CAD (confirmed in the page's JSON-LD, priceCurrency CAD). Re-read 2026-10-08: Bike Weight now listed as 28 kg; 750 W / 1,100 W peak / 75 Nm, 15.2 Ah 730 Wh, 200 kg max load / 30 kg rack, PAS range 129 km; no sale price on the page. Re-verified 2026-10-09 against the live page: CA$2,699.00 CAD, 48V 750W / 1100W peak / 75Nm, 15.2Ah (730Wh) Samsung/LG 21700, pedal-assist range 129 km and throttle range 105 km, 28 kg, Tektro hydraulic disc 180 mm both ends, Class 1/2/3, SensorSwap torque and cadence, 200 kg max load / 30 kg rack. The throttle figure is now quoted in the maker's own current unit (105 km); the earlier 65 mi is the same quantity.

products.motor: 500 W Bafang geared hub (750 W peak)
products.best_for: The long-haul, high-speed pick: the biggest battery here (960 Wh) and the only bike in this set that ships at Class 3, with a 45 km/h claimed top speed. Vancouver-designed, with a 5-year frame warranty. It was Out of Stock when checked.
products.source_note: Product page and its Specifications tab (motor, torque, battery, class, brakes, weight, weight capacity, warranty). Price shown as CA$2,699.00 (page JSON-LD: priceCurrency CAD). This model showed Out of Stock on the date checked. Re-read 2026-10-08: the Specifications tab now publishes 500 W (peaks at 750 W) Bafang geared hub, 65 Nm, net weight 27.75 kg / 61 lb, and weight capacity 300 lb (136 kg). Re-verified 2026-10-09 against the live page: CA$2,699.00, 500W peaking at 750W Bafang geared hub, 65Nm, 48V 20Ah / 960Wh Samsung 21700, up to 150 km eco, 27.75 kg (61 lb), Tektro Auriga hydraulic disc, Class 3 (45 km/h), dropout torque sensor, 300 lb (136 kg) capacity, 5-year frame / 2-year components - all unchanged, still shown Out of Stock.

products.motor: Rear hub, 350 W sustained (540 W peak)
products.range: up to 46 mi / 74 km (maker, Eco mode)
products.brakes: Tektro HD-T280 hydraulic disc, 180 mm rotors front and rear
products.best_for: A flat-city commuter on the lowest budget here: at 46 lb it is light, and it still carries hydraulic disc brakes, a torque sensor and front and rear lights. The 345.6 Wh battery and the maker's own Eco-mode range figure suit short, light trips rather than long ones.
products.source_note: Technical Specifications panel and the feature strip on Aventon's Canadian (en-ca) product page, read 2026-10-08: Speed Class 2, 36 V 350 W sustained / 540 W peak brushless hub motor, Motor Torque 45 Nm, battery 36 V 9.6 Ah (345.6 Wh) with LG cells, Sensors 'Double Sided Bottom Bracket Torque Sensor', Weight 46 lbs, Total Weight Limit 300 lbs, front and rear brake Tektro HD-T280 hydraulic disc with 180 mm rotors, Pedal Assist 4 levels, Front and rear lights integrated, UL 2849 / UL 2271 certified, and the page's own '2 Year Warranty' badge. Range is published as 'Up to 46 Miles' with the page's own footnote: 'Max range is estimated based on a rider weighing 165 lbs (75 kg) on a paved, flat road, in Eco Mode, with Ride Tune set to the default settings.' The miles figure is converted at 1 mi = 1.609344 km and shown as both. Price is the CA$1,699.00 shown on the en-ca page (variants at 169900). Stock wording seen on the page: 'Limited stock available. Order today.' Re-verified 2026-10-09 against the live en-ca page: CA$1,699.00, 350W sustained / 540W peak, 45Nm, 36V 9.6Ah (345.6Wh) LG cells, up to 46 miles (Eco), 46 lbs, Class 2, Tektro HD-T280 hydraulic disc with 180 mm rotors both ends, double-sided bottom-bracket torque sensor, total weight limit 300 lbs, 2-year warranty - all unchanged.

products.motor: Shimano E7000, 250 W continuous / 500 W peak
products.brakes: Shimano MT-420 quad-piston hydraulic disc (180 mm front / 160 mm rear)
products.eclass: 32 km/h speed assist (Canada); no class number published
products.best_for: The comfort-first step-through: an upright position, a Shimano E7000 system with 60 Nm, and a maker that has designed in North Vancouver since 2005 and states a 10-year parts guarantee. It is also the dearest bike on this page.
products.source_note: Technical Specifications accordion and the Bike Details tab on OHM's own product page, read 2026-10-08: Motor 'Shimano E7000, 250W continuous / 500W peak, 60Nm', Battery '504Wh, Li-ion, In-tube, State of Charge Display', Speed Assist '32 km/h (Canada)*' with the page's own footnote ('Motor is rated at 250W continuous output - the legally relevant figure under Canada's federal PAB regulations (500W max). Peak power rating reflects momentary output under load. Speed assist is firmware-configured to 32 km/h for Canadian compliance (28 mph available for US Class 3 regions)'), Brakes 'Shimano MT-420, Quad Piston, Hydraulic Disc' with 180 mm front / 160 mm rear rotors, Frame 'Premium Hydroformed Aluminium, Step-Through', and the page's own '2-Year Warranty' badge. Bike Details: Weight 22.2 kg (49 lb), MSRP $3,499 CAD. Range: the specification table publishes no range figure and names no assist level. Until 2026-10-09 this entry quoted 100 km, from the page's own summary text ('Shimano E7000, 60 Nm torque, 100 km range'); that text is no longer published, and the only range figure the maker now gives on this product page is its own feature tile, "150km Freedom" (read 2026-10-09), so the figure is labelled as coming from that tile. The same page's FAQ answers 'Is it heavy?' with 52 lbs while the Bike Details tab says 22.2 kg (49 lb); the tab figure is the one used here. Price CA$3,499.00 CAD (Shopify product data; storefront currency CAD), 'Add to cart' enabled and no variant flagged sold out. The product page's own name is 'Cruise'; its URL, the maker's comparison page and its city collection call it Cruise 3. Everything else re-verified 2026-10-09 against the live page: CA$3,499.00 CAD, Shimano E7000 250W continuous / 500W peak / 60Nm, 504Wh in-tube battery, 22.2 kg (49 lb), Shimano MT-420 quad-piston hydraulic disc (180 mm front / 160 mm rear), 32 km/h speed assist (Canada), 2-year warranty - all unchanged.
